description: Minimal shared cross-methodology ontology. Symbols here are allowed in IR without methodology-local redefinition.

forbidden: hidden helper concepts invented only for convenience
methodology-specific symbols added to Prelude ad hoc
silent redefinition of Prelude symbols inside a methodology
notes: Event is a generic cross-methodology carrier for dated occurrences.
Organization and Document are general because they appear in any methodology that names actors and references texts (legal, regulatory, clinical, financial). Local entries should NOT redeclare them.

DocumentPart and DocumentLocator are generic provenance carriers for sections, paragraphs, clauses, tables, appendices, and URL fragments. Concrete section names, paragraph numbers, URLs, and document titles remain local.
Period is the temporal abstraction matching `Day`/`Month`/`Weekday` — duration/range over time, used by any methodology with windowing semantics.

LookbackWindow is the shared temporal carrier for backward-looking windows anchored by a methodology-local date or event. Local entries should define source-specific windows such as one-month or six-month lookbacks locally.

WebResource and Url are generic reference carriers. Concrete sites, documents, document parts, locators, and URL values from a methodology should be local entities or provenance/waiver entries, not Prelude entities.

VagueTerm is a generic carrier for source terms that are semantically relevant but underdefined by the text, such as missing thresholds, unspecified standards, or undefined qualitative predicates. Concrete vague terms remain local entities.
FinancialInstrument is general because most evaluated pipelines reference financial instruments at some level.
day_before(Day, Day) is the canonical Day-on-Day temporal ordering. Local entries should NOT declare a generic `before` relation.
Methodology-specific event types such as RebalanceEvent, SelectionEvent, ExtraordinaryRebalanceEvent, TradingDay, RebalanceDay, SelectionDay, FreeFloat, and IndexUniverse do not belong in Prelude.
